reason: Both sell IoT/M2M hardware plus recurring software to enterprise customers. Digi's core is connectivity infrastructure: routers, modules and device management (T:P1.1, T:P1.2). PowerFleet sells subscription-based IoT solutions for tracking and managing enterprise assets (C:S1.1). That makes PowerFleet a vertical telematics and asset-tracking application, not a connectivity-hardware vendor. The product overlap is partial. The customer overlap is partial as well: both serve enterprise and transportation or logistics users, but Digi also sells to OEMs, public sector and network operators.
missing_evidence: Comp evidence is thin (two near-identical web lines). It would help to see PowerFleet's actual device lineup and whether it sells to OEMs or competes with Digi's routers and modules.
